issues.legal_issue: A landlord seeking eviction on a ground established under a rent control statute need not first terminate the tenancy by a notice under the general property-transfer law, unless the rent statute itself requires a notice.
material_facts: The landlord applied to evict the tenant under the applicable rent control statute on the ground of personal necessity.

The appellate court found that the premises were bona fide required for personal necessity but dismissed the application because it considered a notice to quit necessary and the notice given defective.
The High Court held that a notice under the general property-transfer law was not required to seek eviction under the rent control statute.
issues.conclusion: The Supreme Court held that a notice under section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act was not necessary to obtain an eviction order under the rent control statute and affirmed the High Court on that point.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 106 and 111(h) of the Transfer of Property Act, notice may determine a lease where the lease has not otherwise determined. But where a rent control statute permits eviction only on specified grounds, establishing a statutory ground is sufficient; determining the contractual tenancy by a section 106 notice is unnecessary. A notice specifically required by the rent statute must still be given. The Court relied on Rai Brij Raj Krishna v. S. K. Shaw and Brothers, Raval and Co. v. K. G. Ramachandran, Shri Hem Chand v. Shrimati Sham Devi, and Puwada Venkateswara Rao v. Chidamana Venkata Ramana, among other authorities, and rejected earlier decisions on the section 106 notice question, including Bhaiya Punjalal Bhagwanddin, Mangilal, Manujendra Dutt, Isha Valimohamad, P. J. Gupta, Dattopant Gopalyarao Devakate, Ratan Lal, and Sardarilal Vishwanath.

rule.if: rent_control_eviction_proceeding and statutory_eviction_ground_established and tenant_continues_under_rent_act and not rent_act_specific_notice_required

predicates.rent_control_eviction_proceeding: A landlord sought to evict a tenant under a rent control statute.
predicates.statutory_eviction_ground_established: The landlord established a ground for eviction specified by the rent control statute.
predicates.tenant_continues_under_rent_act: The rent control statute treats the occupier as a tenant after contractual termination and limits eviction to statutory grounds.
predicates.rent_act_specific_notice_required: The rent control statute expressly requires a particular notice before the landlord may obtain the relief sought.
predicates.section_106_notice_not_required: The landlord may seek eviction without first giving a notice under the general property-transfer law.

issues.definition: When a landlord seeks eviction under a rent control statute, establishes a statutory eviction ground, and the statute does not require a particular notice, the landlord may proceed without a general property-transfer notice.
